title: When an app is installed from multiple sources, differentiate them somehow
line: When the same app is installed from the distribution and as a Flatpak or Snap, menu search and Open With now label the copies "(Flatpak)" or "(Snap)".
explanation: Distribution, Flatpak and Snap copies of an app use different desktop file ids but the same Name, and every app list showed only the name, so the copies looked identical in menu search, the Open With menu, KIO's Open With dialog and the portal's app chooser (which Plasma and portal-using apps like Thunderbird use for "Other Application…"). Flatpak marks its exported desktop files with X-Flatpak and snapd with X-SnapInstanceName. Each of those lists now finds names used by more than one app and, only for those, appends "(Flatpak)" or "(Snap)" to the copies that carry those keys; the distribution copy and all apps with unique names keep their plain name.

commits.message:
widgets: show where an app comes from when its name is ambiguous

An app installed both from the distribution and as a Flatpak or Snap
had identical entries in the Open With menu and dialog. Those copies now
say (Flatpak) or (Snap) after their name, so they can be told apart.

BUG: 459653

runners/services: show where an app comes from if its name is ambiguous

An app installed both from the distribution and as a Flatpak or Snap
gave several identical search results, so there was no way to tell which
was which. Those copies now say (Flatpak) or (Snap) after their name.

BUG: 459653

appchooser: show where an app comes from when its name is ambiguous

An app installed both from the distribution and as a Flatpak or Snap
showed up several times with the same name in the app chooser, so there
was no way to tell them apart. Those copies now say (Flatpak) or (Snap).
